title: UX rules contract
description: The authored rule layer. A payload writes these; the engine implements detectors against them and takes severity and wording from here. The lifecycle fields (since / deprecated / superseded_by) and the deprecations ledger are what make a rule set safe to change: check-rules-compat reads them to tell a real revision from a silent one.

version.description: Semver for the contract itself. MUST be raised whenever a rule is removed, re-categorised, or has its severity changed — check-rules-compat fails the build otherwise.

severity_levels.description: The severity vocabulary this payload uses, each mapped to what a violation means. The engine maps must/forbidden to error and should/may to warning.

order.description: Categories, most-wins-first. When two rules conflict the earlier category wins.

deprecations.description: The ledger of rules that once existed and no longer do. A removal is legal only if it is recorded here — otherwise a rule can vanish and every consumer's check simply stops testing for it, with nothing to notice.

id.description: The id of the rule that was removed.

since.description: Contract version in which it was removed.

superseded_by.description: The rule id that now covers this ground, if any.

reason.description: Why it went. A removal with no reason is indistinguishable from an accident.

id.description: Stable identifier. Renaming one is a removal plus an addition — record it in deprecations.

severity.description: Must be a key of severity_levels.

label.description: Short human name, shown in reports.

statement.description: What to do, in the imperative. This is the text an agent reads.

rationale.description: Why. Without it the rule cannot be argued with, only obeyed or ignored.

applies_to.description: Graph node ids, or a macro from target_macros. Validated against graph.json as a typo guard.

since.description: Contract version this rule was introduced in.

deprecated.description: Still published and still checked, but on its way out. Prefer superseded_by so readers know where to go.

superseded_by.description: The rule id that replaces this one.
